The test image shows a severely yellowed/browned tomato leaf with large irregular necrotic areas, curled and dying tissue. No powdery coating, no clear concentric rings. Top candidates: Late Blight, Phytophthora Blight, Early Blight.

Now viewing reference images one at a time across different classes:

Having viewed 8 reference images across 8 different classes, here is my analysis:

- **Late Blight** (CDDM_498 and LeafNet_423): Both show large irregular brown necrotic areas on tomato leaves with similar color and pattern to the test image - closest match
- **Phytophthora Blight**: Stem lesions on standing plants - not matching
- **Early Blight**: Circular target spots - not matching
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Small circular dark spots on green leaf - not matching
- **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus**: Whole-plant wilting with dark curled leaves - not matching
- **Verticillium Wilt**: Marginal necrosis with wilting - less extensive than test image
- **Gray Mold**: Fruit rot with gray fuzzy mold - not matching
- **Leaf Mold**: Yellow/pale spots on upper surface - not matching

The test image shows a tomato leaf with large, irregular brown necrotic lesions progressing across much of the leaf with surrounding yellowing and leaf curling. This pattern closely matches the Late Blight reference images, which show the same type of expansive dark-brown water-soaked-to-necrotic lesions with irregular margins.
